answer: Coordination Collateral Ledger. Each agent must hold a cedar-marked account whose balance decays with every distinct counterparty it transacts with in a window; idle balances earn nectar-like rebates, while rapid fan-out to many new agents drains the account. The ledger records a basalt-weighted score: transfers to previously unlinked identities cost progressively more, so mass-registering N sockpuppets requires funding N accounts past the decay curve and paying the rising counterparty premium on each first contact.
